label: UniFi U7 Outdoor
description: Ubiquiti U7-Outdoor - Wi-Fi 7 outdoor AP (IPX6): 2x2 5GHz (4.3 Gbps, 240MHz) + 2x2 2.4GHz, 2.5GbE RJ45 PoE+ uplink.
notes: PoE draw read 2026-11-28 from https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/wifi/u7-outdoor (HTTP 200, 661,328 B): the specification table prints "Power Method: PoE+" and "Max. Power Consumption: 19W". 19 W is that figure and it sits on eth0, the single RJ45 the same table's Networking Interface row names. Until this pass the port carried no poeIn at all, so engine/media.js fell back to its 12.95 W 802.3af class default and the model drew 12.95 W whatever the datasheet said. Nothing in the engine compares a PD's draw with the class its PSE declared, so cabling this AP to an 802.3af port is still accepted; the number changes the budget arithmetic, which is the one thing a PoE lab asks of it. The Power Method row also settles two capabilities the spec omitted: PoE+ is 802.3at, and a box that powers itself from the cable is a poe-pd.
